attempts.errorSummary: Fixed 1 code-defect (duplicate quick-view-add-to-cart-btn testid). Remaining failures are all test-code: the BASELINE_NOISE_PATTERNS regex for the defaultProps warning is missing a space between "release." and "Use", so it never matches the actual console message. This causes assertConsoleErrorBudget() to fail in 7 of 9 tests (E2E-001, E2E-004, E2E-004b, E2E-004c, E2E-005, E2E-007, E2E-008).

2 test-code bugs found in e2e/plp-quick-view.spec.ts. Both failures are in the test assertions, not the implementation code.

Bug 1 (E2E-003, line 277-278): The test monitors ALL HTTP responses matching /baskets/i and asserts zero 4xx/5xx. However, after a successful basket mutation, the SDK's React Query cache invalidation triggers a background GET to /customer/shopper-customers/v1/.../customers/{customerId}/baskets which returns 400 for guest shoppers. This is expected platform behavior — the actual add-to-basket mutation succeeds (modal closes, confirmation modal shows, product-added row visible). The test should either (a) filter to only POST/PATCH basket mutations, or (b) exclude GET /shopper-customers/.../baskets from the monitored responses.

Bug 2 (E2E-006, line 387): The test expects quick-view-add-to-cart-btn to be disabled before a size is explicitly selected. But useProductViewModal fetches the full product detail and ProductView internally auto-selects a default variant when the product loads. The first product on the PLP dresses page has an auto-selected variant, so the button is immediately enabled. The test should either (a) find a product that genuinely starts with no pre-selected variant, or (b) verify disabled state only if the product has multiple required variation attributes and none are pre-selected, or (c) check whether any radio in the size group is already selected and skip if so.

bugs.issue: basketResponses filter catches ALL responses matching /baskets/i in the URL, including background GET /shopper-customers/.../customers/{id}/baskets which returns 400 for guest shoppers. This is SDK auto-refetch behavior (React Query cache invalidation), not a feature bug. The actual add-to-basket mutation succeeds — modal closes, confirmation shows, product-added row is visible.
bugs.fix: Change the response filter on line 261 from `/baskets/i.test(res.url())` to something like `/baskets\/v\d/i.test(res.url()) && !res.url().includes('shopper-customers')` to exclude the getCustomerBaskets auto-refetch. Alternatively, filter to only POST/PATCH methods: `if (/baskets/i.test(res.url()) && ['POST','PATCH'].includes(res.request().method()))`. The intent of the assertion is to verify the add-to-basket mutation succeeds, not to audit every background SDK cache refresh.

bugs.issue: Test expects quick-view-add-to-cart-btn to be disabled before explicitly selecting a size, but ProductView auto-selects the default variant when useProductViewModal fetches full product detail. The first PLP dresses product has an auto-selected variant, so the button is enabled immediately. The test assumption ('before selecting a size, button should be disabled') doesn't hold when ProductView pre-selects a valid variant.
bugs.fix: Before asserting disabled state, check whether a size radio is already selected: `const alreadySelected = await sizeGroup.first().getByRole('radio', { checked: true }).count(); if (alreadySelected > 0) { test.skip(true, 'Product auto-selected a variant — cannot test incomplete selection state'); return; }`. Alternatively, iterate tiles to find one where no variant is pre-selected before asserting the disabled state.
